slides.headline: Both tools are actually really good.
slides.body: Before getting into the nuance, both Clay and Claude Code have serious strengths. The question isn't which one is 'better', it's which one fits what you're trying to build.

slides.headline: Clay has a few core moats.
slides.body: A marketplace of data providers that's really hard to compete with. Platform engineering that can run 100k+ API calls at once. And a compliant interface for building GTM workflows that isn't relying on AI for the whole thing.

slides.headline: But Claude Code has huge strengths too.
slides.body: The most powerful AI models in the world. Workflows that run really cheaply. And you can connect tools and data providers (Supabase, Sheets, whatever) in minutes without much work.

slides.headline: Here's where it gets tricky though.
slides.body: Can enterprise really connect their Salesforce to a Claude-built workflow and trust it? Personally, I don't think so. Same story for Snowflake, Outreach, and anything else that holds critical data.

slides.headline: My conclusion?
slides.body: Right now, not a great replacement for enterprise. Too many compliance problems, tracking issues, and variability. For startups running simple enrichment or a ton of actions in one table, Claude and a few good APIs can absolutely get the job done.
